question:
What are some ways to handle the stress and fatigue from taking on every detail of a major community project myself, without ending up completely drained?

Which of these four candidate replies is the best, most personalized response for me? Answer with the single letter (A, B, C, or D) of the best option.

(A) Given your past challenge with not delegating in your company, it may help to frame parts of the community project as ‘design briefs’ you give to others rather than you executing them yourself. That way, you still set the standard and creative direction, but you’re not carrying the physical and mental load of every single detail.

(B) Since you’ve experienced exhaustion and anxiety before from trying to personally oversee every aspect of your business, try setting clear ‘non-negotiable’ boundaries on which elements of the project you truly need to control versus those you can hand off. You might still keep the final approval role, but let trusted collaborators handle the preliminary legwork so you can conserve energy for the areas that really need your expertise.

(C) Because taking on every detail in your business has previously left you fatigued and anxious, consider building ‘micro-teams’ for the project with clear milestones. You can check in at defined points without monitoring every step, which can help prevent the all-consuming involvement that’s worn you down before.

(D) To avoid burnout when leading a big community project, try deciding early which parts you most want to be personally involved in, and delegate the rest to capable team members. By focusing only on the tasks you enjoy or excel at, you preserve your energy and keep motivation high throughout the project.
gold_answer: D — To avoid burnout when leading a big community project, try deciding early which parts you most want to be personally involved in, and delegate the rest to capable team members. By focusing only on the tasks you enjoy or excel at, you preserve your energy and keep motivation high throughout the project.
